newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends steady in abbreviated trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends steady in abbreviated trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished steady on Tuesday in the last trading day of the year in an abbreviated session. Players were sitting on the sidelines waiting to leave their offices for the long New Year holidays, dealers said.
"There was some buying, particularly for RSS3 rubber and some RSS1 rubber, but everything else was dead," a local rubber dealer said. "We just killed the time before taking off."
The Singapore rubber futures market will be closed on Wednesday, January 1, for New Year and on Thursday for Singapore's general elections. The market will reopen on Friday.
Volume reached only 2,740 tonnes against a total trade of more than 4,000 tonnes yesterday.
"There were just some people winding up their positions, but little of anything else," one trader said.
At the close at 0400 GMT, March RSS3 settled unchanged at 127.00 U.S. cents a kg.
April/June RSS1 settled slightly higher at 184.00 Singapore cents (US$1.31) a kg from 183.50 cents.
January TSR20 settled unchanged at 169.75 Singapore cents (US$1.21) a kg.
